text:
Sam Dickinson is one of the fastest skaters in the NHL, faster than 99% of the league by NHL Edge, and at 20 he's playing about 18 minutes a night on the Sharks' blue line. The 11th pick of 2024 scored 91 points in his final season with the London Knights, so the offense is in there. So far this season it's three points in 17 games.

That's a bit behind the curve. Defensemen picked 6th to 16th since 2005 averaged 0.25 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.18 this year after a decent rookie season. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.1 wins last season, 63rd among defensemen, but noted his results ran well ahead of his chances.

The good news is the five-on-five picture: San Jose is about five points of expected goal share better with him on the ice than off. The work in progress is breakouts, with Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking showing only 30% of his exits keeping possession. He scored against Calgary on Nov. 2 and talked afterward about the team working through early frustrations. Our range says 11 to 24 points over a full season. The skating gives him a high floor; the points will follow the puck play.
headline: Dickinson, all skating and patience
